title: Medicaid Services Investment and Accountability Act of 2019
official_summary:
Medicaid Services Investment and Accountability Act of 2019

This bill alters several Medicaid programs and funding provisions.

(Sec. 2) The bill temporarily extends the applicability of Medicaid eligibility criteria that protect against spousal impoverishment for recipients of home- and community-based services.

(Sec. 3) The bill also establishes a state Medicaid option to provide for medical assistance with respect to coordinated care provided through a health home (i.e., a designated provider or team of health-care professionals) for children with medically complex conditions. States must determine payment methodologies in accordance with specified requirements; payments also temporarily qualify for an enhanced federal matching rate.

(Sec. 4) The bill also temporarily extends the Medicaid demonstration program for certified community behavioral health clinics.

(Sec. 5) The bill increases funding available to the Money Follows the Person Rebalancing Demonstration Program. (Under this program, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services may award grants to state Medicaid programs to assist states in increasing the use of home and community care for long-term care and decreasing the use of institutional care.)

(Sec. 6) Further, drug manufacturers with Medicaid rebate agreements for covered outpatient drugs must disclose drug product information. Manufacturers are subject to civil penalties for knowingly misclassifying drugs. Manufacturers are also required to compensate for rebates that were initially underpaid as a result of misclassification (whether or not such misclassification was committed knowingly).

summary.headline: This 2019 law makes several changes to Medicaid, including temporary extensions, a new state option for children with complex medical needs, more funding for moving people from institutions to home care, and new drug-reporting rules for manufacturers.
summary.what_it_does: It temporarily extends Medicaid spousal impoverishment protections for people getting home- and community-based services. It lets states cover coordinated care through a health home for children with medically complex conditions, with payments that temporarily get a higher federal matching rate. It also temporarily extends a Medicaid demonstration program for certified community behavioral health clinics and adds funding to the Money Follows the Person program, which helps people move from institutional care to home and community care. Drug manufacturers with Medicaid rebate agreements must also disclose drug product information, face civil penalties for knowingly misclassifying drugs, and repay underpaid rebates caused by misclassification.

who_it_affects.group: People receiving Medicaid home- and community-based services and their spouses
who_it_affects.how: Spousal impoverishment rules that limit how a spouse's income and assets are counted are temporarily extended for these recipients.

who_it_affects.group: Children with medically complex conditions and their families
who_it_affects.how: States gain an option to cover coordinated care through a designated health home for these children.
States may choose the new health home option and must set payment methods that meet the law's requirements.
Their Medicaid demonstration program is temporarily extended.

who_it_affects.group: People in long-term care who could move from institutions to home or community care
who_it_affects.how: More federal grant funding is available to states through the Money Follows the Person program to support these transitions.

who_it_affects.group: Drug manufacturers with Medicaid rebate agreements
who_it_affects.how: They must disclose drug product information, face civil penalties for knowingly misclassifying drugs, and must pay back rebates that were underpaid due to misclassification, whether or not it was intentional.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on April 18, 2019, and the summary does not give specific effective dates or end dates for the temporary extensions.
